interpretation.scope: Each profile applies independently to its listed BOM models. Source paths resolve at repository root against docs/reference/manifest.json. Page numbers are one-based in that PDF. Fields inherit the register's source, table, owners, reset context, prerequisites and release policy.
interpretation.behavior: docs/device-behavior.md defines timing and read-effect policy. docs/registers/behavior-vectors.json supplies independent numerical cases and event traces.
interpretation.numbers: Addresses and positioned masks are unsigned JSON integers. Field factory and encoding values are unshifted. Whole-register factory values refer to TI's stated reset on factory settings. Limits, offset and EEPROM-eligible settings may already have been programmed. Uncertain or conflicting defaults are written out.
interpretation.nvm_mask: Register-positioned bits eligible for EEPROM storage in the silicon. Zero means the field is outside that storage domain. All release operations leave NVM unprogrammed.
interpretation.policy: observe permits a read of a hardware read-only register. deny-write permits observation and refuses all data writes even if hardware is R/W. guarded permits only the named typed volatile mutation after its prerequisites. mixed CONFIG separates status, stable settings and explicit commands. No public raw data writes.
interpretation.safety: docs/eeprom-and-reset-policy.md defines startup, the operation-local guard, fail-closed EUN handling, protected shadow access, reset and outside interference.
interpretation.owners: Numbers identify forward stages for implementation and verification. The feature matrix records the evidence level per row and model.

protocol.pointer: Power-up pointer 0x00. Device retains the last selected pointer. Reject a reserved or out-of-range selector before I/O; never truncate upper bits. Register auto-increment is undocumented.
protocol.read_word: START, address+W, pointer, repeated START, address+R, MSB (controller ACK), LSB (controller NACK), STOP.
protocol.write_word: START, address+W, pointer, MSB, LSB, STOP; target acknowledges address and bytes. Only typed, guarded volatile writes are permitted by release policy.
protocol.timeout_condition: SDA release without clocks. Between START and STOP the controller holds SCL low or the target holds SDA low. Timeout resets the serial interface.
protocol.stop_behavior: Source documents timeout recovery; STOP-triggered state-machine reset unconfirmed.
protocol.ownership: Target never drives SCL. Application and adapter own clock, electrical timing, routing, serialization and bounded callback deadlines. The interface timeout is distinct from transfer and conversion budgets.

startup.writes: All register writes ignored during the initial load. Reads are possible.
startup.policy: When startup proof is absent, begin/recover timestamps completion of its first successful compatible read. Wait at least 3 ms from FIRST_ACK, allowing for clock resolution (library policy), require continuous stable power and verify owned writes. Reuse proof under continuous power/ownership until invalidated. A ready guard word cannot substitute for this wait. Each managed mutation or fresh acquisition then checks 0x04 for locked and idle.

registers.name: TEMP
registers.reset: Holds 0x8000 until the first conversion including averaging completes. The bit pattern alone cannot establish validity or freshness.
registers.read: Returns the reset word until the first completed block, then the latest result. Consumes DATA_READY and leaves HIGH/LOW intact. An update during the two-byte read has unspecified latching. A failed read may already have consumed readiness.
registers.write: No writable field.
registers.prerequisites: Bound to a BOM-selected target on a known route. Use an explicit pointer and one complete word.

fields.name: T
fields.read: Signed two's-complement counts in units of 1/128 degree Celsius. Code range is -256 to +255.9921875 degrees Celsius. Measuring range and grade are separate.
fields.write: No writable field.

registers.name: CONFIG
registers.reset: POR and documented general-call reset load the programmed MOD0 and bits 9:2. MOD1, status, commands and reserved bits are outside that NVM domain.
registers.read: Consumes DATA_READY in both modes. In alert mode, retain returned HIGH/LOW on every successful CONFIG read, including diagnostics, verification and late reads, which acknowledge the hardware latches. In therm mode HIGH is a hysteresis level and LOW is zero. A failed read can leave flag history uncertain.
registers.write: Apply only owned stable fields. Keep commands and reserved bits out of replay. MOD=11 belongs to an explicit one-shot. Addressed reset is unavailable.
registers.prerequisites: Bound target for status observation. For mutation, establish startup readiness, serialize the target, and check EEPROM_UL in this operation for EUN=0 and BUSY=0. Reuse the guard only within this uninterrupted operation. Ambiguous writes invalidate affected trust; any subsequent busy observation invalidates the guard.

fields.name: HIGH
fields.read: Alert mode latches a result above THIGH until acknowledgement by CONFIG read. In therm mode HIGH sets above THIGH, holds in band including equality, and clears below TLOW on conversion comparisons.
fields.write: No writable field.

encodings.1: latched high alert or active therm level

fields.name: LOW
fields.read: Alert mode latches a result below TLOW until acknowledgement by CONFIG read. In therm mode LOW reads zero.
fields.write: No writable field.

fields.name: DATA_READY
fields.read: Set on TEMP update at the end of a nonoverlapping block. CONFIG or TEMP read clears this one-bit indication. Updates can coalesce. The exact clear edge relative to a concurrent update is unspecified.
fields.write: No writable field.

fields.name: EEPROM_BUSY
fields.read: Observed busy during programming. Startup indications disagree between the overview and field tables. Mirrors EEPROM_UL bit 14. Observing busy invalidates the current operation's locked/idle guard.
fields.write: No writable field.

fields.name: MOD
fields.read: Writing binary 10 selects continuous conversion and reads back 00. One-shot MOD readback during and after conversion is unspecified.
fields.write: Only MOD0 (bit 10) is EEPROM-storable. Stable profile modes are continuous and shutdown. An owned one-shot requires a guarded shutdown write and status baseline, then one trigger.

encodings.3: one-shot from shutdown, physical return to shutdown after completion

fields.name: CONV
fields.read: Read the current field value.
fields.write: Select the nominal continuous cycle. AVG sets a lower limit on the period. One-shot duration is independent of CONV.
fields.cycle_basis: Nominal continuous period including active time, indexed by CONV code (row) and AVG code (column). The rounded 125/500/1000 ms cells do not specify maxima. Standby is zero where active time fills the period.

fields.name: AVG
fields.timing_condition: One conversion. Multiply each value by the block count for a derived active interval.
fields.read: Read the current field value.
fields.write: Select conversions per accumulated block, with one TEMP update at completion.

fields.name: THERM

fields.write: Apply through a guarded volatile CONFIG write.

fields.write: Select polarity of the open-drain output. The board supplies the pullup.

fields.write: Select the ALERT pin source.

registers.prerequisites: Bound to a BOM-selected target on a known route. Use an explicit pointer and one complete word.

fields.name: T
fields.read: Signed two's-complement counts in units of 1/128 degree Celsius. Code range is -256 to +255.9921875 degrees Celsius. Measuring range and grade are separate.
fields.write: No writable field.

registers.name: CONFIG
registers.reset: POR and documented general-call reset load the programmed MOD0 and bits 9:2. MOD1, status, commands and reserved bits are outside that NVM domain. Addressed Soft_Reset reload effects remain unknown.
registers.read: Consumes DATA_READY in both modes. In alert mode, retain returned HIGH/LOW on every successful CONFIG read, including diagnostics, verification and late reads, which acknowledge the hardware latches. In therm mode HIGH is a hysteresis level and LOW is zero. A failed read can leave flag history uncertain.
registers.write: Apply only owned stable fields. Keep commands and reserved bits out of replay. MOD=11 belongs to an explicit one-shot. Bit 1 belongs to explicit addressed reset with verified stable settings and canonical continuous/shutdown mode. Invalidate startup, guard and affected trust before the command. No ordinary CONFIG or recovery write sets bit 1.
registers.prerequisites: Bound target for status observation. For mutation, establish startup readiness, serialize the target, and check EEPROM_UL in this operation for EUN=0 and BUSY=0. Reuse the guard only within this uninterrupted operation. Ambiguous writes invalidate affected trust; any subsequent busy observation invalidates the guard.

fields.name: HIGH
fields.read: Alert mode latches a result above THIGH until acknowledgement by CONFIG read. In therm mode HIGH sets above THIGH, holds in band including equality, and clears below TLOW on conversion comparisons.
fields.write: No writable field.

encodings.1: latched high alert or active therm level

fields.name: LOW
fields.read: Alert mode latches a result below TLOW until acknowledgement by CONFIG read. In therm mode LOW reads zero.
fields.write: No writable field.

fields.name: DATA_READY
fields.read: Set on TEMP update at the end of a nonoverlapping block. CONFIG or TEMP read clears this one-bit indication. Updates can coalesce. The exact clear edge relative to a concurrent update is unspecified.
fields.write: No writable field.

fields.name: EEPROM_BUSY
fields.read: Observed busy during programming. The POR overview and field table describe busy during startup load. Mirrors EEPROM_UL bit 14. Observing busy invalidates the current operation's locked/idle guard.
fields.write: No writable field.

fields.name: MOD
fields.read: Writing binary 10 selects continuous conversion and reads back 00. One-shot MOD readback during and after conversion is unspecified.
fields.write: Only MOD0 (bit 10) is EEPROM-storable. Stable profile modes are continuous and shutdown. An owned one-shot requires a guarded shutdown write and status baseline, then one trigger.

encodings.3: one-shot conversion, physical return to shutdown after completion

fields.name: CONV
fields.read: Read the current field value.
fields.write: Select the nominal continuous cycle. AVG sets a lower limit on the period. One-shot duration is independent of CONV.
fields.cycle_basis: Nominal continuous period including active time, indexed by CONV code (row) and AVG code (column). The rounded 125/500/1000 ms cells do not specify maxima. Standby is zero where active time fills the period.

fields.name: AVG
fields.timing_condition: No internal averaging. Multiply each value by the block count for a derived active interval.
fields.read: Read the current field value.
fields.write: Select conversions per accumulated block, with one TEMP update at completion.

fields.name: THERM
fields.read: Read the current field value.
fields.write: Apply through a guarded volatile CONFIG write.

fields.name: POL
fields.read: Read the current field value.
fields.write: Select polarity of the open-drain output. The board supplies the pullup.

fields.name: DR_ALERT
fields.read: Read the current field value.
fields.write: Select the ALERT pin source.

fields.name: SOFT_RESET
fields.read: Always reads zero, including after a command. This bit cannot confirm completion.
fields.write: Write 1 issues the addressed 2 ms software reset. Ordinary CONFIG writes emit zero. EUN, EEPROM reload, companion bits and bus availability remain unknown. Wait from successful transfer completion before post-reset observations. Later writes require new FIRST_ACK, startup readiness and a fresh safe guard.

fields.name: RESERVED
fields.read: TI lists unused bits with reset value zero. Ignore these bits when interpreting the word.
fields.write: Write zero when constructing a CONFIG word.

registers.name: THIGH
registers.reset: Power-up and documented general-call reset reload the programmed word from EEPROM. A previous owner may have changed startup contents or the current volatile shadow.
registers.read: Read the high comparison threshold shadow. Signed two's-complement counts in units of 1/128 degree Celsius.
registers.write: With EEPROM locked, writes update the volatile shadow. With EEPROM unlocked, writes can program NVM.
registers.prerequisites: Bound target for shadow reads. For mutation, establish startup readiness, serialize the target, and check EEPROM_UL in this operation for EUN=0 and BUSY=0. registers.name: EEPROM_UL
registers.reset: Locked at power-up. BUSY is live status. The documented general-call reset reloads programmed values and relocks EEPROM. General-call traffic is excluded.
registers.read: Read one complete word for EUN and BUSY together without acknowledging CONFIG flags. Lock must be known and both bits clear. With EUN clear and BUSY set, only timed, paced 0x04 observations may continue within deadline and work cap. A transport failure ends the attempt.
registers.write: The release denies every data write to this pointer, including relock.
registers.prerequisites: Bound to a BOM-selected target on a known route. Use an explicit pointer and one complete word.

fields.name: EUN
fields.read: Reads the current unlock state. Observed EUN=1 fails closed until application power cycle or authorized external relock, followed by invalidation and verified recovery.
fields.write: Silicon accepts lock control. The driver only observes it.

fields.name: BUSY
fields.read: Observed busy during programming. The POR overview and field table describe busy during startup load. Mirrors CONFIG bit 12.
fields.write: No writable field.

fields.name: RESERVED
fields.read: TI lists unused bits with reset value zero. Ignore these bits when interpreting the word.
fields.write: No writable field.

registers.name: EEPROM1

registers.read: Read one volatile EEPROM data shadow. Accept any 16-bit value, including zero. Current contents alone cannot authenticate factory data or prove physical NVM contents.
registers.write: With EEPROM locked, writes update the volatile shadow. With EEPROM unlocked, writes can program NVM. Deny every data write to the shadow including through diagnostic, job and CLI paths, even when locked.

sources.claim: Reset-load overview describes EEPROM_UL busy as clear during load.

conflicts.policy: A clear bit cannot prove startup completion. Require readiness evidence and an operation-local lock/busy check before mutation.

sources.claim: Map gives zero for EEPROM1 through EEPROM4.
Detailed tables show unknown for EEPROM1, EEPROM2 and EEPROM4, and zero for EEPROM3.
Factory traceability information occupies these data locations.

conflicts.policy: Observe arbitrary contents in all four shadows; preserve them. Document factory table values separately from programmed startup and measured contents.

Electrical specifications, operating prose and pinned orderables extend to +125 degrees Celsius.

sources.claim: Pin description and functional circuit use an external pullup for ALERT.
